What if you never wore sunscreen?
Many people only put on sunscreen at the beach. You might just get a nice tan. UV rays reach your skin even on cloudy days.

But here's the twist. Up to ninety percent of visible skin aging, like wrinkles and dark spots, comes from the sun, and a study found daily sunscreen users had no detectable increase in skin aging! Dermatologists say use SPF thirty or higher every day, and reapply every two hours outside. Sunscreen also lowers your risk of skin cancer, the most common cancer in the United States.
